script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Saying the test is about what the idols can say ahead of time leaves out the challenge to tell the former things, which the explanation itself mentions.
The passage gives a verdict but does not say there can be no appeals or second hearing.
“Wrong compass” uses “wrong” about the baker’s answer, which Papa Dorin must not do.
The explanation is flat and repetitive. “That’s what the verse says” adds no personality or insight.
“I’d have loved a comeback too” assumes the baker wanted a comeback, although Papa Dorin has not been told that.
The definition suggests that the idols only look real and do not exist. The verse calls them a delusion and speaks of their images; it does not say the images do not exist.
